### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

Having a dataframe that contains NAN or None values, sorting treats those as smallest values.
In many situations this can be undesired.

I think it would be great to have them always at the bottom of the sorted column, regardless of sorting order, either by changing the default behavior or by having an option in `st.dataframe`.

Example:
```python
import streamlit as st
import pandas as pd

df = pd.DataFrame({
    "A": [1, 3, None, 2, None],
    "B": [1.5, None, 5.2, 8.9, None]
})
st.dataframe(df)
```

PS:
I brought this up in the [forum](https://discuss.streamlit.io/t/ignore-none-nan-values-in-st-dataframe-sorting/107715) and it was suggested to put this in as a feature request.

### Why?

Having columns that correspond to some kind of ranking, e.g. accuracy or an error metric, having `None`'s show up on top when sorting is irritating. In many cases one is not interested in the None columns and having them sorted at the end, regardless whether sorting ascending or descending, would clear up the visualization.

### How?

Either change the default behavior or add a `na_position="last"` option to `st.dataframe` in accordance with the same option in pandas dataframe `sort_values`.

### Additional Context

_No response_
issues.title: Put `None`'s at bottom when sorting dataframe columns with `None` values

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

During a full-script rerun, a callback is often used to modify a widget's value before it's rendered on the page. However, during a fragment rerun, any widget that does not exist within that widget should not be modifiable. The fragment rerun does not stale and redraw widgets that live outside the fragment (and we disallow a fragment from displaying widgets outside of its main body).

However, in the case of a fragment rerun, if we modify a non-fragment widget through Session State, no error is raised. The value in Session State is silently updated and becomes out-of-sync with its associated element on the front end.

We should ensure that all non-stale widgets raise an error if their value is modified in Session State.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import streamlit as st

def set_main():
    print("set main")
    st.session_state.main = 10

st.number_input("Main", key="main")

@st.fragment
def frag():
    st.number_input("Frag", key="frag", on_change=set_main)
    st.session_state.main
    st.session_state.frag

frag()
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Run the app
2. Click `+` on the "Frag" widget.
3. Observe no change in the "Main" widget, no error, and a new value for `st.session_state.main`.

### Expected Behavior

If you try to modify Session State for a widget and that widget exists on the frontend (not stale), Streamlit should raise an error.

### Current Behavior

In the case of a fragment rerun, no error is raised when trying to manipulate the value of a widget outside of the rerunning fragment.

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version:
- Python version:
- Operating System:
- Browser:


### Additional Information

_No response_
issues.title: Streamlit fails to raise an error when modifying non-fragment widget values in a fragment rerun

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

The key algorithm in `_make_funcion_key` used by `cache_data` does not consider free (aka non-local) variables of a function.

Therefore the wrapper function `cache_data` creates may return incorrect results in cases like:

- 2 inner functions created with the same code but captured different outer values (see repro in OP)
- any function captured an altering variable in its closure (see https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/11157#issuecomment-2822938487 )

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import streamlit as st
from streamlit.runtime.caching.cache_type import CacheType
from streamlit.runtime.caching.cache_utils import _make_function_key


def create_cached_inner_function(a: int):
    def inner_function(b: int):
        return f"a={a} b={b}"

    return _make_function_key(CacheType.DATA, inner_function), st.cache_data(
        inner_function
    )


key1, cached_func1 = create_cached_inner_function(1)
key2, cached_func2 = create_cached_inner_function(2)

st.write(f"create_cached_inner_function(1)(1): {repr(cached_func1(1))}")
st.write(f"create_cached_inner_function(2)(1): {repr(cached_func2(1))}")

assert key1 == key2
```

### Steps To Reproduce

run the page

### Expected Behavior

the page should look like

```
create_cached_inner_function(1)(1): a=1 b=1

create_cached_inner_function(2)(1): a=2 b=1
```

and fail with AssertionError

### Current Behavior


```
create_cached_inner_function(1)(1): a=1 b=1

create_cached_inner_function(2)(1): a=1 b=1
```

and no AssertionError arises

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.44.1
- Python version: 3.13.2
- Operating System: ArchLinux
- Browser: any


### Additional Information

A perfect fix is beyond my limited knowledge. Current version already uses function metadata including `func.__code__`, and they don't help to distinguish in this case.

Are there other elements we can use?
issues.title: `cache_data` cannot detect difference in values of free variables, or 2 inner functions with identical __qualname__

### Checklist

- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

I implemented this simple function to wrap `n` columns into multiple rows:
```python


def wrapped_columns(n: int, wrap=4, divider=False, **kwargs) -> list[DeltaGenerator]:
    """Create n columns, wrapping them every `wrap` columns. Each row will always have `wrap` columns

    :return: flat list of n columns
    """
    assert isinstance(n, int), "n must be an integer"
    rows = n // wrap + (1 if n % wrap > 0 else 0)
    columns = []
    for row in range(rows):
        if row != 0 and divider:
            st.divider()
        for c in st.columns(wrap, **kwargs):
            if len(columns) == n:
                break
            columns.append(c)
    return columns
```

This will create n columns, wrapping them every `wrap` columns, optionally with a `st.divider()` in between.

It can be used like this:

```python
elements = ... # some elements to be visualized
for zip(elem, col) in zip(elements, wrap_columns(len(elements), 4)):
    with col:
        st.write(elem)
```

### Why?

I can use my `wrapped_columns` function, but without that wrapper it's actually quite tricky to achieve and might not be obvious to most users.

### How?

This could be added directly into `st.columns` as `wrap` and `wrap_divider` arguments.

### Additional Context

_No response_

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

With the introduction of `accept_new_options`, Streamlit uses the string value instead of the index internally to track selections. This means repeated labels aren't supported anymore

### Reproducible Code Example

[![Open in Streamlit Cloud](https://static.streamlit.io/badges/streamlit_badge_black_white.svg)](https://issues.streamlitapp.com/?issue=gh-11219)

```Python
import streamlit as st

class foo():
    def __init__(self, a):
        self.a = a
    def __repr__(self):
        return "foo " + self.a
    def __str__(self):
        return self.a

options = [foo("a"),"a"]

c = st.multiselect("C", options=options)
c

b = st.multiselect("D", options=["A", "B", "B", "C", "C", "C"])
b
```

### Steps To Reproduce

- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

If you change any parameter of a widget in Streamlit (e.g. the label or the default value), Streamlit will treat it as a new widget and reset its state. That’s necessary because we determine which widget state belongs to which widget based on the parameters. (Note that there are a few exceptions to this rule, e.g. changing the `disabled` parameter will not reset the widget). 

But we still do this when you manually set `key`! Even though in that case, we can easily associate the widget state with the widget based on the `key`. We should change that and always preserve the widget identity if `key` is set. 

### Why?

This (potentially) fixes lots of small issues such as:

- https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/1532
- https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/4854
- https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/6352
- https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/7054
- https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/7749

### Summary

Add an option to disable LaTeX rendering page wide using `.streamlit/config.toml` file.

### Why?

LaTeX is great for describing mathematical formulas, but I guess a very large percentage of all Streamlit pages ever created doesn’t have that kind of content. A more common content would be a dollar sign - $ - and unfortunately this breaks markdown formatted text. A workaround is to escape the dollar sign with backslash – `text.replace("$", "\$")` – but this is cumbersome if you have a complex page.  
The issue has been discussed in #7638 where the developers have hinted about a way to disable LaTeX rendering using a parameter `extensions` but it's unclear how strings with $ would be rendered in other situations when markdown is rendered except `st.markdown`. Therefore, using the settings would be more convenient.

### How?

Add an option to disable LaTeX rendering page wide in the `.streamlit/config.toml` file.

### Additional Context

_No response_

### Summary


The existing column configuration in (editable) dataframes are a really nice and powerfull feature already. However, I think the data_editor can become even more powerfull if column config arguments can be set on the row level, meaning that arguments can be dependent on other columns (in the same row). 

In short, I think the following addition would be great:

Adding **row specific** dynamic column configuration.


### Why?

Obviously this does not mean that one row can be a number, and the next a selectbox column type. I would like to keep the "one column, one type" logic, like it is right now. However I believe that the arguments of that column configuration should be able to change dependent on other columns in the same row. 

An example:
Lets say we have two dropdown columns: Continent and Country. I think it would be great if these could be linked to each other. If I select Europe as Continent, it would be great if I only see European countries in the country column (for that row). In the next row, I should be able to select Asia, and only see Asian countries in the Country column instead. If I have not selected a Continent, all countries should be available.

I could think of similar links between other types of columns:
- two date columns that use the input of column one as value for the min_value or max_value argument in the second date column
- a checkbox column that allows changing of individual cells in that specific row (setting the disabled argument to true or false)

surely I'm missing out of more really cool applications in addition to these couple of examples. 



### How?

I think this might link to [this issue](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/7057), where also column values are created based on other columns. 

I also don't really have a clue how to implement this. I guess there needs to be something like an input_columns argument in order to "link" a column to other columns. Then those inputs can flow into a function a user defines himself, in order to get back the actual arguments that are required. 

For example:

Min_number is a column that contains a number. 
Max_number is a column that depends on the Min_number column, and should at least be 2 times as large.

In the column_config of the Max_number, there is an argument input_columns that is set to [Min_number]. The min_value argument of the Max_number column could then be set to input_columns[Min_number]*2

issues.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

st.expander() is documented to accept a key parameter since Streamlit v1.10.0 (PR #4290). However, when installing various Streamlit versions (tested 1.10.0 through 1.45.1) via pip on Python 3.13.2 (64-bit) on Windows 10, the actual source code for the expander method within the distributed wheel files on PyPI does not include the key parameter. This results in a TypeError when attempting to use this documented feature.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import streamlit as st
import inspect # For further debugging if needed by maintainers

st.set_page_config(page_title="Expander Key Test")
st.write(f"Streamlit version: {st.__version__}")

st.subheader("Attempting to use st.expander with 'key'")

try:
    with st.expander("Test Expander with Key", key="my_expander_key_123"):
        st.write("This content should appear if 'key' is supported.")
    st.success("st.expander with 'key' parameter was accepted.")
except TypeError as e:
    st.error(f"TypeError encountered: {e}")
    st.subheader("Signature of st.expander from this environment:")
    if hasattr(st, 'expander'):
        st.code(str(inspect.signature(st.expander)))
    else:
        st.write("st.expander not found.")
else:
    st.write("No TypeError, but please verify 'key' functionality if this message appears without error.")

st.subheader("Attempting st.expander WITHOUT 'key'")
try:
    with st.expander("Test Expander without Key"):
        st.write("This content will appear.")
    st.success("st.expander WITHOUT 'key' parameter works as expected.")
except Exception as e:
    st.error(f"Error with expander without key: {e}")
```

### Steps To Reproduce

Set up an environment with Python 3.13.2 (64-bit) on Windows 10.
Ensure no conflicting Python installations (e.g., disable Microsoft Store app execution aliases for python.exe, python3.exe).
In a clean virtual environment (or global, though the issue persists even in venvs):
pip install --no-cache-dir streamlit==1.45.1 # (or 1.44.0, 1.39.0, down to 1.10.0)
Use code with caution.
Bash
Run the "Reproducible Code Example" above as a Streamlit app.
Observe the TypeError for the expander using the key parameter.

### Expected Behavior

When running the reproducible code example with Streamlit versions >= 1.10.0, the st.expander("Test Expander with Key", key="my_expander_key_123") call should execute without a TypeError, and the expander should be rendered, respecting the key for state management if applicable. The inspect.signature(st.expander) should show key as an accepted parameter.

### Current Behavior

TypeError: LayoutsMixin.expander() got an unexpected keyword argument 'key'


### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

It's unclear if it's a recent regression or a long-standing packaging discrepancy. Testing with an advanced_wheel_inspector.py script (see Gist linked in Additional Information) on wheels downloaded directly from PyPI shows the key parameter missing from the expander source code in streamlit/elements/layouts.py for versions 1.45.1, 1.44.0, 1.39.0, 1.35.0, 1.30.0, 1.25.0, and even 1.10.0 when wheels for Python 3.13/Windows are inspected. This suggests the key parameter may have been missing from the distributed code for st.expander for these combinations for a long time, despite being documented and intended since PR #4290.

Streamlit version: Tested 1.45.1, 1.44.0, 1.39.0, 1.35.0, 1.30.0, 1.25.0, 1.10.0 (all from PyPI)
Python version: 3.13.2 (64-bit, CPython from python.org)
Operating System: Windows 10 Pro
Browser: Chrome

### Additional Information

Official Documentation for st.expander (shows key parameter):
[https://docs.streamlit.io/library/api-reference/layout/st.expander](https://www.google.com/url?sa=E&q=https%3A%2F%2Fdocs.streamlit.io%2Flibrary%2Fapi-reference%2Flayout%2Fst.expander)

GitHub PR #4290 introducing key to st.expander for v1.10.0:
[https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/4290](https://www.google.com/url?sa=E&q=https%3A%2F%2Fgithub.com%2Fstreamlit%2Fstreamlit%2Fpull%2F4290)

advanced_wheel_inspector_v2.py Gist:
https://gist.github.com/PyPIPuzzle007/3436ad13181555741cbafcc26c7ebbdf

Summary of advanced_wheel_inspector_v2.py findings:

The script directly downloaded and extracted .whl files from PyPI for the listed Streamlit versions. For all tested versions (1.10.0 through 1.45.1), inspection of the streamlit/elements/layouts.py (or equivalent) source file within the wheel showed that the def expander(...) signature and its implementation did not include the key parameter. This indicates a discrepancy between the documented/intended API and the code being distributed in the wheels selected by pip for Python 3.13 on Windows.

advanced_wheel_inspector_v2.py findings/wheel_inspector_output.txt Gist:
https://gist.github.com/PyPIPuzzle007/2519e0c84df10c30d90f9f6b5bd5cb5f
issues.title: Discrepancy: st.expander key parameter missing in distributed wheels (e.g., v1.10.0 - v1.45.1 for Python 3.13/Win) despite documentation and PR #4290

### Summary

My usecase (simplified):

I pull a table from a database into a data editor. Columns ID (Primary Key), NAME (Alternate Key), DISPLAY_NAME.
The data_editor num_rows is st to “dynamic”.

I set the NAME column in the data editor to disabled=True because nobody should update the alternate key once it is created. Some other systems may depend on it.

But when creating a new row in the data_editor I have to enter it, because its a key, but this is blocked by the disabled=True flag



### Why?

It blocks me from using the data_editor as a true database table editor

### How?

Suggestion for column config flags:

st.write(f"The version of Python is {sys.version}.")

st.dataframe(pkg_resources.working_set) # Or setuptools

### Checklist

- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

Provide a component that will trigger a server-side render when it receives a message from a specified websocket server.

### Why?

Currently, streamlit requires an execution-flow, that starts in the browser. Usually, the user is interacting with a component (e.g. changing the value of input components, or pressing buttons, etc...), which triggers a render operation on the server-side. As a result of this paradigm, it is difficult to implement flows, that start with the server sending a push event to the client.

Some examples would be:

- A chatroom where the server notifies each of the participants that a new message was sent
- A live presentation where the presenter wants to push updates to all viewers, e.g. for highlighting some of the presented data, or for "changing to the next slide" by triggering a rerun that renders a new layout
- A dashboard that displays the current state of a system, which only changes sporadically and with long time-periods in between

All of these examples can be solved by polling for updates in an infinite loop, e.g. by using third-party components like [streamlit-autorefresh](https://github.com/kmcgrady/streamlit-autorefresh). The issue with this approach is that it results in a lot of wasted computation and requests where a rerun is triggered without any changes occurring. This also doesn't scale well with more and more session-threads.

This polling approach can be avoided by adding a component that only triggers a server-side rerun when it receives a websocket message on the client-side. The currently implemented execution-flow stays the same, since everything starts with a change on the client-side. 
But instead of requiring a user-interaction like a button-click, a websocket server can trigger it remotely.

### How?

On the python side, the implementation could look very similar to any of the existing input-widgets:

```python
# allow for http-header customization to enable authentication and individualized socket connections
raw_message: bytes = st.websocket_receive(url="https://some-websocket-server-address", http_headers={"Authorization": "Basic ..."})
# directly receive strings
# message: str = st.websocket_receive(url=..., encoding="utf-8")

# everytime a socket-message was received, this should trigger a redraw that shows the received message
st.write(raw_message.decode("utf-8"))
```

On the client side, the component would open a websocket using the specified URL and header fields and will update the component value as soon as it receives a message. *(I am not really familiar with js/ts... so I can't provide example code for this part of the implementation)*

## Added Bonus:

With such a component, the [multithreading section](https://docs.streamlit.io/develop/concepts/design/multithreading) in the docs could also be updated with an additional example. Instead of having to join the worker-thread, it could be a deamon that starts a websocket-server and asynchronously communicates with the streamlit app via the proposed websocket component.

## Notes on Security

The proposed implementation requires the client to know both the URL and the custom header fields, and it should be highlighted in the documentation that those should only contain values that the client is allowed to know about.

### Additional Context

Issue #2927 proposes a very similar approach but also provides a [solution](https://github.com/FloWide/streamlit_callbacks/tree/main) that only uses websockets on the server-side, which doesn't really solve the polling issue. As far as I can tell, they added the socket-listener thread to the ScriptRunContext which can result in unexpected behavior and fatal errors and may not work for all streamlit commands *(according to the [multithreading documentation](https://docs.streamlit.io/develop/concepts/design/multithreading))*. What I want to propose instead, is an implementation that starts at the client-side and fits more to the currently supported execution flow of streamlit apps.
issues.title: Websocket Notify component to allow for Push-Notifications without polling

issues.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

**Issue Description:**

When a user edits cells in the `st.data_editor` object, the `on_change` callback function is triggered. If the user makes additional edits while the `on_change` callback is still running, some edits are processed multiple times (in this case, twice for edits of the first interaction and once for the second interaction) when using the `session_state` of the `st.data_editor` to process the user edits. This occurs because the callback is threaded, and the `session_state` of the `st.data_editor` object still includes the edits from the previous user interaction.

**Additional Issue:**

Attempting to fix this revealed another issue: If the `on_change` callback for a previous call takes longer to execute than the latest call, the Streamlit page reloads before the previous `on_change` callbacks are finished. As a result, not all cells of the `st.data_editor` object are updated, leading to potential loss of user edits. This seems to be fixed by using `threading.Lock()` in the on_change callback function.

**Request:**
I found a solution to this, but would like to know if I just use the `st.data_editor` object and corresponding `on_change` callback in a way that they were not meant to be used (passing/using the `session_state` of the `st.data_editor` in the callback).
-> Is there another method to handle user edits on a dataframe, which ensures that those edits are processed exactly once, so neither multiple times nor never before the Streamlit page or `st.fragment` get reloaded?

### Why?

This is relevant when streaming user edits to a backend database, as potentially user edits are send multiple times to the backend, which causes unnecessary traffic, or edits are lost and not sent to the backend at all.

### How?

Solution (including filtering of the `st.data_editor`'s session state and locking threads during the `on_change` callback):
```python
import streamlit as st
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import threading
import time

st.set_page_config(layout="wide")

# Initialize session state variables if not already done
if "applied_edits" not in st.session_state:
    st.session_state["applied_edits"] = {}
if "df" not in st.session_state:
    data = np.zeros((1000, 30))
    columns = [f"Column {i + 1}" for i in range(30)]
    df_init = pd.DataFrame(data, columns=columns)
    totals_row = pd.DataFrame(df_init.sum(axis=0)).T
    st.session_state.df = pd.concat([totals_row, df_init], ignore_index=True)
    st.session_state.df["Totals"] = st.session_state.df.sum(axis=1)
if "call" not in st.session_state:
    st.session_state["call"] = 0
if "lock" not in st.session_state:
    st.session_state["lock"] = threading.Lock()


def df_on_change(df):
    with st.session_state["lock"]:
        print(f"on_change call: {st.session_state['call']}")
        # Get a copy of all edited rows in this session
        all_edits = st.session_state["df_editor"]["edited_rows"]
        # Filter out the new edits/changes that were/are not processed in a previous call of the df_on_change function
        edited_rows = {
            row: {
                col: val
                for col, val in changes.items()
                if (row not in st.session_state["applied_edits"])
                or (st.session_state["applied_edits"][row].get(col) != val)
            }
            for row, changes in all_edits.items()
        }
        # Update the record of applied edits so the filter above can be applied in the next call of the df_on_change function once again
        for row, changes in edited_rows.items():
            if not changes:
                continue  # no new changes for this row
            if row not in st.session_state["applied_edits"]:
                st.session_state["applied_edits"][row] = {}
            for col, val in changes.items():
                st.session_state["applied_edits"][row][col] = val

        # Log the filtered edits for debugging
        print(f"session state of data editor: {st.session_state['df_editor']}")
        print(f"New edits to apply: {edited_rows}")
        print(f"Applied edits history: {st.session_state['applied_edits']}")

        # Apply the new changes to the DataFrame
        for row, changes in edited_rows.items():
            for col, val in changes.items():
                print(f"writing value {val} to row {row} and column {col}")
                df.loc[row, col] = val
                # simulate a on_change function that requires a long execution time
                time.sleep(1)

        # Recompute totals row based on all data below it
        df.loc[0] = df.iloc[1:].sum(axis=0)
        df["Totals"] = df.sum(axis=1)

        st.toast("Data updated successfully!")
        st.session_state["call"] += 1


# Use st.data_editor with the on_change callback
st.data_editor(
    st.session_state.df,
    use_container_width=True,
    num_rows="fixed",
    disabled=["Totals"],  # prevent editing the totals row
    column_order=[f"Column {i + 1}" for i in range(30)] + ["Totals"],
    key="df_editor",
    on_change=df_on_change,
    args=[st.session_state.df],
    row_height=20,
)
```

In the demo videos below, the user first adds 9 cells at once and then does single cell changes afterwards (on other cells).

Demo video of the code above (terminal output also shows that each edit/cell is just processed once, which is not the case when not filtering the `st.data_editor`'s session state):

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9e924ae7-4cc0-4c96-8029-97c98f872548

Demo video without thread locking:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/aac91a5d-536c-4a44-97c0-1219d80684af

### Additional Context

_No response_
issues.title: Concurrency issues with `st.data_editor` `on_change` callback: Using the `session_state` of the `st.data_editor` leads to multiple processing or potential data loss

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

Streamlit’s st.login() (introduced in ≥1.42.0) simplifies OpenID Connect authentication by wiring up a ready-made OAuth2/OIDC client under the hood. However, it currently only reads a fixed set of configuration values—namely:


    server_metadata_url

    client_id

    client_secret

    redirect_uri

    (optional) cookie_secret


All other request details (scopes, prompt, response type, audience, login hints, PKCE settings, etc.) are either hard-coded or not exposed to the end user. This limitation forces developers who need slight variations—such as adding custom scopes, changing the prompt mode to consent, specifying an audience, or tweaking PKCE parameters—to drop down to a lower-level library (Authlib, requests-oauthlib) and lose the convenience of st.login().

### Why?

- st.login() always injects the literal scopes "openid email profile".

- No documented way to override or extend scopes, nor to add any other OAuth2/OIDC parameters (e.g. prompt, response_type, audience, login_hint, code_challenge_method, token_endpoint_auth_method, etc.).

- Any attempt to pass additional values via client_kwargs, secrets, or env vars is ignored.



### How?

**Provide a flexible mechanism for developers to supply any standard (and future) OAuth2/OIDC parameters to st.login(), not just the core five:**

1. Extend the signature of st.login() to accept a well-documented set of optional keyword arguments (or a single client_kwargs: dict parameter).
2. Merge any supplied parameters with sensible defaults when constructing the authorization URL and token request.
3. Ensure backward compatibility by preserving the existing default values if no overrides are provided.
4. Update the API reference, examples, and streamlit_app.py templates to illustrate how to customize scopes, prompts, audiences, PKCE, and other common OIDC/OAuth2 options.

**This could take one or more of these forms:**

New keyword arguments on st.login(), e.g.:

```Python
st.login(
  server_metadata_url=…,
  client_id=…,
  client_secret=…,
  redirect_uri=…,
  # NEW: override or extend default scopes
  scopes=["openid", "roles", "profile"],
  # NEW: pass arbitrary OIDC query params
  prompt="consent",
  audience="https://api.myservice.internal",
  login_hint="user@example.com",
  response_type="code",
  code_challenge_method="S256",
)
```

A catch-all client_kwargs dict that is forwarded to the underlying OAuth2/OIDC client, for instance:

```Python
st.login(
  …,
  client_kwargs={
    "scope":            "openid roles profile",
    "prompt":           "consent",
    "audience":         "https://api.myservice.internal",
    "code_challenge_method": "S256",
  }
)
```



Support in secrets.toml or env vars for any of these parameters:

```Toml
[streamlit]
server_metadata_url  = "…"
client_id            = "…"
client_secret        = "…"
redirect_uri         = "…"
scopes               = "openid roles profile"
prompt               = "consent"
audience             = "https://api.myservice.internal"
code_challenge_method = "S256"
```


### Additional Context

Use Cases


- Retrieving additional claims or roles using custom scopes (roles, groups, etc.).
- 
- Forcing the user consent screen (prompt=consent) on every login.
- 
- Targeting a specific resource server or audience (audience=…).
- 
- Pre-filling hints for login (login_hint).
- 
- Enabling or customizing PKCE (code_challenge_method="S256").
- 
- Supporting advanced token endpoint auth methods (e.g. token_endpoint_auth_method="private_key_jwt").
- 
- Allowing future extension as new OIDC/OAuth2 parameters emerge without breaking API.



Thank you for considering this enhancement! Happy to provide a proof-of-concept PR or further implementation details.
issues.title: Allow advanced customization of OIDC/OAuth2 parameters in st.login()

### Summary

Add an optional zebra_stripe parameter to st.dataframe() to enable alternating row background colors, improving readability for large datasets.

### Why?

## Problem: 
Large dataframes displayed in Streamlit can be difficult to read when rows blend together visually, especially with many columns or when users need to track data across rows.
Benefits:

- Improved readability - Alternating row colors help users follow data horizontally across columns
- Better UX - Common UI pattern that users expect in data tables
- Accessibility - Reduces visual strain when scanning tabular data
- Professional appearance - Matches styling conventions in modern data applications

##Use cases:

- Financial reports with many numerical columns
- Large datasets where row tracking is important
- Dashboards requiring professional table presentation
- Any scenario where dataframe readability is crucial

### How?

## Proposed API:
```python
st.dataframe(df, zebra_stripe=True)  # Enable alternating row colors
st.dataframe(df, zebra_stripe=False)  # Default behavior (no stripes)
```

## Implementation approach:

- Add zebra_stripe boolean parameter to the st.dataframe() function
- Pass this parameter to the frontend dataframe component
- Apply CSS styling for alternating row backgrounds (e.g., nth-child(even) selector)
- Ensure compatibility with existing styling options

### Summary

width 现在只支持 stretch or int，更应该支持float(0, 1]。宽度占用parent container的百分比更好用，因为不同用户的屏幕大小不一致，通过固定像素太死板了，无法适配所有的屏幕。如果一些元素没使用width,一些使用了width=int(xx)，非常容易导致布局混乱。

`Width` parameter now only supports `stretch` or `INT`, float(0,1] should be supported. The width as a percentage of the parent container works better because the screen size varies from user to user, and fixing pixels is too rigid to fit on all screens. If some elements don't use `width`, and some use `width = int (xx)` , it's easy to get cluttered.



### Why?

_No response_

issues.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

I cannot edit the Contribution documentation directly to propose changes, because it is a "wiki" page https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/wiki/Contributing I don't have edit access to instead of living directly in https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/develop/CONTRIBUTING.md

Here are my suggestions based on my struggles building Streamlit on Ubuntu WSL:

https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/wiki/Contributing#ubuntu should have the additions:

* If you are on Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS or earlier, then you will only have access to libprotoc 3.12.4, which is lower than the minimum required version 3.20. Therefore, you will have to `do-release-upgrade`. *(This one could be edited to have the weasel word "might" instead of "will" if you don't believe very strongly in the validity of the detective work I did months ago.)*

* Make sure you have sudo installed. This comes with Ubuntu by default; but if you somehow lack it, you can become root using `su -` and then install sudo with `apt-get install -y sudo`. *(This one is of questionable usefulness, but for some reason I did need to do this at some point.)*

* If you get an error like `error: failed to remove file [blah blah blah]/streamlit/.venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/streamlit-1.43.2.dist-info/INSTALLER: Permission denied (os error 13)`, try running `sudo chmod -R 777 .venv` first, and/or prefix your `make` command with `sudo`, eg `sudo make all`. *(This one could be moved to the section that talks about WSL, I suppose, since I don't know if this issue ever arises on native linux (I've only run everything through WSL so I don't know what happens on not-WSL).)*

https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/wiki/Contributing#windows should have the addition:

* WSL2 is more likely than WSL1 to work, as there is (or, at least, has been) a [binary compatibility problem](https://github.com/microsoft/WSL/issues/8151) between nodejs and WSL1.

https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/wiki/Contributing#2-grab-the-code should have the addition:

* For implementation reasons, the absolute filepath of the Streamlit directory must not contain any characters that are specially interpreted by the shell. (The shell in question is almost certainly [Bash](https://www.gnu.org/software/bash/manual/bash.html).) *(~~If #11741 and #11742 get fixed then this advice will become obsolete.~~ Edit: unfortunately, this one will not be obsolete until https://github.com/protobufjs/protobuf.js/issues/2081 (a thing with a similar problem, that we depend upon internally) is also fixed, and there is little momentum there. Edit 2026-04-29: that was fixed two days ago, so whenever you get on the current version of that dep special characters are back on the menu...!)*
* **(new)** Independent of the previous warning, there should be a warning: Due to [internal implementation reasons](https://nodejs.org/api/esm.html#resolution-algorithm-specification), the absolute filepath of the Streamlit directory must not contain any backslashes.

### Why?

WSL is not officially supported, but neither is it officially anathema, so I'm happy to share these hard-won tips I discovered. Some of the other info relates to platforms that are officially supported.

### How?

You may copy these all verbatim or change them in any way you like. I release all of that text I wrote into the public domain and also the license of this project. Feel free to close this issue when you've determined you've taken all that you want.

### Additional Context

**Trivia**

These tips mostly come from stuff I discovered while working on https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/10829, which was in turn something I started while trying to start working on a pull request for some other feature that I actually wanted.

**Contribution License Agreement**

By submitting this issue I agree that all contributions to this project are made under the Apache 2.0 license.

issues.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

As soon as I tried to submit a score for the previous answer, the generation of the current answer would stop immediately. This happened even though I wasn’t touching the generation logic directly. The simple act of submitting feedback caused the interruption in the in-progress generation

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import streamlit as st
import random
from langchain_core.messages import AIMessage, HumanMessage

# Set page config and title
st.set_page_config(page_title="Random Chat Assistant", page_icon="💬")
st.title("Random Chat Assistant")

# Initialize chat history
if "chat_history" not in st.session_state:
    st.session_state.chat_history = [
        AIMessage(
            content="Hello! I'm a random response bot. Ask me anything.",
            feedback_requested=False
        )
    ]

# Display past chat messages
for message in st.session_state.chat_history:
    role = "ai" if isinstance(message, AIMessage) else "human"
    with st.chat_message(role):
        st.write(message.content)
        if isinstance(message, AIMessage) and message.feedback_requested:
            feedback = st.feedback(
                options="faces",
                key=f"feedback_{id(message)}",
                kwargs={"log_object_id": id(message)}
            )
            if feedback:
                st.toast(f"Feedback submitted: {feedback}")

# Input box for user
user_input = st.chat_input("Type your question here...")

if user_input:
    # Add user's message
    st.session_state.chat_history.append(HumanMessage(content=user_input))
    with st.chat_message("human"):
        st.write(user_input)

    # Generate a random AI message
    fake_responses = [
        "That's an interesting question!",
        "Let me think... probably yes.",
        "Hmm, I don't have that information right now.",
        "Sure, here’s a random idea: try googling it!",
        "This sounds like a job for StackOverflow."
    ]
    ai_reply = random.choice(fake_responses)

    with st.chat_message("ai"):
        import time
        time.sleep(2)
        st.write(ai_reply)
        score = st.feedback(
            options="faces",
            key=f"feedback_ai_{len(st.session_state.chat_history)}",
            kwargs={"log_object_id": f"fake_{len(st.session_state.chat_history)}"}
        )
        print("Score: ", score)
    st.session_state.chat_history.append(
        AIMessage(content=ai_reply, feedback_requested=True)
    )
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Run the code `streamlit run file_name.py`
2. Write the first random message
3. Write the second random message, and immediately score the first response
4. See that the response generation is interrupted

### Expected Behavior

The response generation must not be interrupted.

### Current Behavior

_No response_

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.46.0
- Python version: 3.9.6
- Operating System: Linux
- Browser: Chrome


### Additional Information

_No response_
issues.title: Submitting Feedback for Previous Answers Interrupts Ongoing Answer Generation

### Summary

We allow specifying pixel widths/heights for many elements, e.g. `st.dataframe(..., width=500, height=300)`. Today, these widths always stay at the same pixel size. Should we adjust them if you change the `baseFontSize`, so they work a little bit more similar to `rem`? Or should we allow specifying `rem` (and `em`) directly, e.g. `width="10rem"`?

### Why?

1. The elements with custom width/height will work better with different themes then. Note that we already adjust the sizes of other elements to the `baseFontSize`. 
2. For accessibility, it's better if everything adjusts to the base font size, e.g. if that is set to a higher value by the browser.

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

I’d like to request a feature to add support for anchor tags in Column Configuration when rendering a dataframe, which would allow jumping to other parts of the same webpage very quickly.




### Why?

Currently, streamlit can do quite a lot to deal with URLs, but only if they are external links. Anchor links are a type of interior link that appends a `http://<url>#<section_name>` to the current URL and jumps to that location. Anchor links are not supported by the current version of Link Column, since it will take any given link and instead make it `http://<url>/#<section_name>`. That extra slash after `<url>` means its looking for a whole new webpage.

I can get similar capability in st.table, however I lose out on the nice styling and other capabilities of an st.dataframe, such as applying other column configurations.

### How?

I’m wondering if this could be achieved either by modifying LinkColumn to allow for anchor tags as an input argument with accompanying logic, or perhaps a new Column Configuration type such as one specifically for anchor tags or one that works with markdown, which would be allow the user to generate links using markdown.

### Additional Context

_No response_
issues.title: Add support for anchor tag hyperlinks in Column Configuration for st.dataframe

issues.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

Already asked in the forums: [How to Detect onRender Events Triggered by Resize in Custom Streamlit Components?](https://discuss.streamlit.io/t/how-to-detect-onrender-events-triggered-by-resize-in-custom-streamlit-components/111226)

So, we render streamlit apps in an iFrame inside our main application with a communication bridge using post-robot. Our SDK is declared as custom components so we can use it to invoke different methods. And we need to find a sure fire way to differentiate between renders due to resizing and actual backend code re-execution so our API methods can skip such re-renders without complete memoization for every re-render.

**Now the problem is that:**

 - Even resizing the sidebar triggers a streamlit:render event with no way of distinguishing between a resize or call being made from the backend.

**We’ve tried:**

 - Looking for differences in the event object, found none.
 - Checking if our event.detail.args.params keyword param (dict from the backend) is the same object reference but it’s new every time.
 - Passing an ever changing call_id param down from python wrapper (component function) to track changes (hoping to detect a backend event vs resize) but this causes an infinite loop.


**Present workaround is to:**

Do deep equality check on params+key and not re-trigger if the params+key remain the same. Meaning the developers would need to change the key/param in order to execute the same method again. **Example:**

```python
if st.button("View details"):
    desktop.open(OpenParams(records=Entity(**entity_dict)))
```

If a user presses the button multiple times, multiple tabs won’t open. But they will open if they interact with something else in between (desktop.open is un-mounted). And if we don’t do this equality check based memoization then they’ll get a new tab even upon resizing the window depending on what they interacted with before. This makes the app behaviour very non deterministic.


### Is this a regression?

- [ ] No, this has been the behaviour.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.33.0
- Python version: 3.9
- Operating System: MacOS
- Browser: Chrome


### Additional Information

_No response_
issues.title: No way to Detect onRender Events Triggered by Resize in Custom Streamlit Components

### Summary

Only literal comparison is used to enforce file extension restriction.

This possible today via the `markdown` library but it's a bit awkward because of how `st.sidebar` works. ```python import markdown def generate_toc(md_text): md = markdown.Markdown(extensions=['toc']) md.convert(md_text) return md.toc docs = "# Some lengthy Markdown document loaded from a file..." toc = generate_toc(docs) with st.sidebar: st.markdown( "## Table of Contents\n\n" + toc, unsafe_allow_html=True, ) st.markdown(docs) ``` If the rest of your app doesn't use or need a sidebar, suddenly having one just for your docs creates a slightly jarring shift in content as you navigate between doc and non-doc pages. It's also a bit inconvenient to have to install and use separate library just to generate a handy table of contents, which feels like it should be common enough a use case to be part of Streamlit's built-in Markdown tools. ### How? Best would be to have some kind of floating sidebar on the right for the table of contents, like how Streamlit has [in its own docs](https://docs.streamlit.io/develop/concepts/architecture/app-chrome): I could see this working via some new parameters to `st.sidebar` to place it on the right and give it the same background as the main content. Perhaps cleaner would be a dedicated new `st.toc` widget just to generate a table of contents that floats on the right like in Streamlit's docs. ```python # render a TOC for all headings/Markdown on the current page st.toc() # render a TOC for the given Markdown content st.toc(markdown_content) # render a TOC only for the top-level headings st.toc(level=1) ``` ### Additional Context #3704 is related but that's about adding support for the non-standard `[toc]` directive. ### Summary

Currently, the `st.context.ip_address` feature will _always_ return `None` if you're using a proxy or load balancer because Streamlit doesn't set the Tornado server's `xheaders` setting to `True`. Therefore, even if you correctly configure the `X-Forwarded-For` and `X-Real-Ip` headers on your proxy, `st.context.ip_address` will never work because the Tornado server isn't configured to observe those headers. (And currently can't be configured, except via some elaborate monkey patching.)

In other words:
* `st.context.ip_address` relies on Tornado's [remote_ip](https://www.tornadoweb.org/en/stable/httputil.html#tornado.httputil.HTTPServerRequest.remote_ip) feature.

* → When [Streamlit initialises the Tornado server](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/1.46.0/lib/streamlit/web/server/server.py#L138-L142) it doesn't pass that setting.

* → 😭 

I think the solution is a simple one-line change to pass `xheaders=True` when creating the `tornado.httpserver.HTTPServer` instance.

issues.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

We have `st.session_state` which allows us to manage widget values. I'm proposing an interface to work with frontend states.


### Why?

We recently introduced a pattern for setting the placeholder text of `st.chat_input`. We used `st.session_state` to do this, but the pattern is very different of other uses because `st.chat_input` is more like a trigger than a stateful widget.

It seems more scalable to have a separate interface for "setting stuff on the frontend but not implicitly sending the information back to the Python server or triggering a rerun."

### How?

`st.frontend_state` would have similar access as `st.session_state`: for example,
* `st.frontend_state.<element_key>.focus()` would be a command to set focus on the frontend.
* `st.frontend_state.<element_key>.state("collapsed")` or `state("expanded")` could be available for the sidebar or expanders. (We set the initial state from the backend, but users are free to expand or collapse these items from the frontend without triggering a rerun.)
* `st.frontend_state.<element_state>.disabled(True)` or `disabled(False)` could be used to disable widgets at the beginning of a run and re-enable them at the end of a run if you want to prevent script run interruptions. (As an auto-protection, any widget that is enabled within the widget command but disabled through frontend state must automatically be re-enabled at the end of a script run if the developer didn't do so themselves.)

The idea of `st.frontend_state` would be to cause state changes that don't themselves cause reruns or otherwise report to the Python backend. (Edgecase: If a use has focus on a widget and a partial edit, then forcing focus elsewhere should technically cause a rerun and submit that partial edit, so app developers would be responsible for using focus appropriately.)

### Additional Context

`st.frontend_state` takes inspiration from both `st.session_state` and `AppTest`. It could be used for two-way communication, but be much less restrictive than Session State. That is, there'd be no problem calling it multiple times. You could "retrieve" the current frontend state multiple times if you wanted to detect if the user had expanded/collapsed something in the middle of a rerun. Unlike states that immediately trigger a rerun and are more rigidly controlled within a script run, the "frontend only" states can be set and retrieved multiple times during a run, in general.

Another example: suppose `st.tabs` gets an `on_change` parameter. `on_change="ignore"` is the default and it operates as it does currently, with the tab selection being a frontend state. If we set `on_change="rerun"` or assign a callable, it becomes a widget. In the first case, you could access or set the current tab through `st.frontend_state` (and not impact the flow of the rerun). In the latter case, the selection is a "value" that must be controlled through `st.session_state`, not `st.frontend_state`.
issues.title: Create an interface to manage frontend state

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

Streamlit supports static image serving with https://docs.streamlit.io/develop/concepts/configuration/serving-static-files but using the static path does not work for:
- st.image
- st.chat_message(avatar)
- st.set_page_config(page_icon)

And I guess every other API does accept AtomicImage.

### Why?

Serving images over static path is way more efficient than as it is today in st.image under the hud system that will read the file, try to understand what it is, resize it, and then keep a local copy. All this work is not necessary for static images.

On the other side, being able to provide a static image without knowing where the server is running is essential to reduce complexity. As of now, the only workaround is to build a valid URL to the app/static path.

```python
curent_url = get_current_url_somehow()
st.chat_message(..., avatar = f"{curent_url}/app/static/my_image.png")
```

### How?

The static path is well-known, so it would be easy to add in the processing of AtomicImage a check for it before continuing.

### Additional Context

_No response_
issues.title: static images served by streamlit should work on all image compatible features

issues.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

Since the last update from Streamlit 1.45.1 (Tornado 6.4.2) to 1.47.0 (Tornado 6.5.1) my users reported very frequent (say every half a minute) grey-outs of the pages/elements. Upon further inspection it seems that the websocket connection was often considered closed.

The cause seems to lie in the `ping_timeout` saga (https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/3196, https://github.com/tornadoweb/tornado/pull/3376, https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/11670).

Forcing Tornado to 6.4.2 (while still keeping streamlit on 1.47.0) solves the issue because the conditional sets the `websocket_ping_interval` to 1s again. We run Streamlit in a Docker container with Nginx, so a proxy setup applies.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
n/a
```

### Steps To Reproduce

Streamlit 1.47.0 in a Docker container with Nginx

### Expected Behavior

Stability with a higher `websocket_ping_interval` server setting (e.g. 30s).
Allowing for more recent versions of Tornado (> 6.4.2) to be used.

### Current Behavior

Streamlit instability with a higher `websocket_ping_interval` server setting

### Is this a regression?

- [x] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.47.0
- Tornado version: 6.5.1
- Python version: 3.12.5
- Operating System: Linux


### Additional Information

Originally this Streamlit issue https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/3196 was reported and solved/merged with `"websocket_ping_interval": 1` on 23 jun 2021.

A recent Tornado issue on https://github.com/tornadoweb/tornado/pull/3376 came to disallow the `websocket_ping_interval` to be below the `websocket_ping_timeout` of 30s. This update was merged/released on 22 april 2025 (Tornado 6.5.1). 

The Tornado update - allowing the `websocket_ping_interval` gave trouble to some Streamlit users, reported 17 jun 2025: https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/11670. This Streamlit issue was eventually solved by the current code: `"websocket_ping_interval": 1 if is_tornado_version_less_than("6.5.0") else 30,`
With the update, @lukasmasuch remarked: `This could potentially bring back an old issue with dropping connections in specific proxy setups - #3196. Something we need to watch out for after this gets released.`

It seems our Streamlit setup is suffering from this regression. Forcing Tornado to 6.4.2 (while still keeping streamlit on 1.47.0) solves the issue because the conditional sets the `websocket_ping_interval` to 1s again.
issues.title: Frequent websocket connection drops on higher (default 30s) ping_interval

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

Currently, the CI fails a check if `ruff format --check` fails, thus preventing poorly-formatted code from making it into the codebase, which is good. However, the CI should simply make the reformatting commit for the user. This is almost always desireable. And, in rare cases when it's not desireable, the user can always rollback the automatic commit and manually add the noqa comments they will need, or whatever, so no harm no foul.

### Why?

Dev QoL

### How?

I think mypy achieves this with a "pre-commit" github action, but there are probably a couple ways.

### Additional Context

Here's an example from mypy, for reference https://github.com/python/mypy/pull/19494/commits/7f102209eaab90297b6bbac4066419accc281050

I run afoul of lint rules all the time, because I don't care about code line length at all and just keep typing; so I love it when the reformatter just takes care of it without complaint, according to the preferences of the repo owner. The popular python reformatters I know about (ruff, black) are also 100% safe in the sense of never changing code meaning by reformatting (except for the occasional formatter bug). There may be security implications for hooking up this action, altho' probably not more than hooking up other actions.
issues.title: Automatically reformat in CI on lint failure

### Why?

> For st.button, I have the following use case: As most of my pages have several filter options and selections, I added a feature to create and store a link in my database that contains the information for a specific page, including all filter settings (it is not possible to keep that in the URL itself). issues.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

`st.plotly_chart` accepts `**kwargs` but with the exception of the `config` parameter these are actually never used in our code. I think we should get rid of them. 


### Why?

Today, you can pass arbitrary `**kwargs` to `st.plotly_chart`, which, according to our documentation, gets passed through to Plotly's `plot()` function. However:

- That's not the case. We only extract a `config` parameter from `**kwargs` (see [here](https://plotly.com/python/configuration-options/)) and pass that through. Additionally, we extract `show_link` and `link_text` and put that into `config` if available, but according to our telemetry data, these parameters are basically never used. 
- The `plot()` function from Plotly mentioned in our docs is outdated. The modern alternative is `show()`. 
- Accepting arbitrary `kwargs` is messy. E.g. right now we're trying to add `width` and `height` to `st.plotly_chart` but some users are already setting these parameters through `kwargs`, probably because they think they get passed through to Plotly. While it doesn't cause any problem in this case, it's better to avoid such problems in the future. 

### How?

I'd suggest we:

- Mark `**kwargs` as deprecated and potentially remove it soon. I.e. this should raise a deprecation warning whenever you pass a parameter not explicitly supported. 
- Add `config` as an explicit parameter and say that this is the Plotly config dict, which is getting passed to the `show()` function. 

### Additional Context

_No response_
issues.title: Deprecate `**kwargs` in `st.plotly_chart` and add `config` instead

issues.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

Add native real-time collaboration functionality enabling multiple users to interact with the same Streamlit app simultaneously. Users can join collaborative sessions via room IDs with automatic widget state synchronization across all participants. This addresses the #1 most requested community feature for 2+ years.

### Why?

I'm always frustrated when trying to use Streamlit for team collaboration scenarios. Currently, Streamlit apps are single-user experiences which creates major bottlenecks for:

**Team Workflows**: Data science teams cannot collaboratively explore dashboards, requiring awkward screen-sharing or separate instances
**Enterprise Adoption**: Companies need multi-user capabilities for business dashboards but Streamlit lacks this fundamental feature
**Interactive Presentations**: No way to create presentations where audience members can participate and see real-time updates
**Educational Use**: Teachers cannot create interactive classroom experiences where students collaborate on the same interface

This limitation has been the top community request across multiple GitHub issues with 500+ combined upvotes over 2+ years. Current workarounds require complex custom infrastructure that most users cannot implement.

The 28,000+ GitHub stars and massive community demand demonstrates this is a critical missing capability preventing wider Streamlit adoption in enterprise and educational environments.


### How?

Introduce a new command called `st.collaborate()` with the following implementation:

### Core API
```python
import streamlit as st

# Enable collaboration with simple API call
user_id = st.collaborate(room_id="team-analytics-session")
st.write(f"👤 Connected as: {user_id[:8]}...")

# All widgets with keys automatically sync across users
dataset = st.selectbox("Dataset", ["sales", "users"], key="shared_dataset")
date_range = st.date_input("Date Range", key="shared_dates")  
budget = st.slider("Budget", 0, 100000, key="shared_budget")
```

### Technical Implementation
- **WebSocket backend** for real-time bidirectional communication
- **Automatic widget synchronization** for all widgets with `key` parameters
- **Room-based isolation** ensuring sessions don't interfere
- **JWT authentication** with configurable security settings
- **Redis persistence** (optional) for scalable multi-server deployment

### Parameters
```python
st.collaborate(
    room_id: str,                    # Required: Unique room identifier
    user_id: Optional[str] = None,   # Optional: User ID (auto-generated if None)
    max_users: int = 50,             # Optional: Maximum room size
    jwt_secret: Optional[str] = None, # Optional: Custom JWT secret
    redis_url: Optional[str] = None   # Optional: Redis connection for persistence
)
```

### Backward Compatibility
- Zero breaking changes to existing apps
- Collaboration is entirely opt-in via `st.collaborate()` call
- Non-collaborative apps have no performance impact
- Graceful degradation if WebSocket unavailable

### Security Features
- JWT-based authentication with configurable expiry
- Rate limiting (10 messages/second per user, configurable)
- Input validation against XSS and injection attacks
- Encrypted data transmission for sensitive content

This would enable powerful use cases like collaborative data analysis, interactive team presentations, shared parameter tuning, and educational applications while maintaining Streamlit's simplicity.


### Additional Context

This feature request is based on extensive community demand:

**Community Sources:**
- Multiple GitHub issues requesting collaboration features with 500+ combined upvotes
- Consistent requests in Streamlit forums and Discord over 2+ years
- Enterprise users citing multi-user capability as adoption blocker

**Related Issues:**
- Similar requests have appeared across community channels asking for "multi-user Streamlit"
- Educational users specifically requesting collaborative classroom capabilities
- Business users needing team dashboard functionality

**Implementation Feasibility:**
I have developed a complete proof-of-concept implementation demonstrating:
- Production-ready WebSocket infrastructure with 50+ concurrent user validation
- Enterprise-grade security with JWT authentication and rate limiting  
- Comprehensive test suite with 92% coverage across security, performance, and functionality
- Zero breaking changes integration approach preserving backward compatibility
- Complete integration guide for core team adoption

**Business Impact:**
- Removes #1 barrier to enterprise Streamlit adoption
- Enables new market segments: collaborative BI, interactive education, team analytics
- Provides competitive advantage over static dashboard solutions
- Addresses most requested community feature spanning 2+ years

The technical implementation is proven feasible with a working prototype that demonstrates enterprise-scale performance, security, and seamless integration with existing Streamlit architecture.
issues.title: Native Real-Time Collaboration - st.collaborate() API

### Checklist

- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

**Description:**  
Currently, Streamlit's `st.tabs()` does not support dynamically updating tab titles without resetting the selected tab. In applications where the tab title needs to reflect real-time counts (e.g., number of items, unread notifications, or messages), updating the title causes the tabs to re-render completely, and the first tab becomes selected by default.  

This makes it difficult to provide live feedback to users without disrupting their current view. A few potential solutions could be:  

1. **Built-in badge support:** Allow tabs to display a small badge (count or indicator) alongside the title, which can be updated dynamically without affecting the selected tab.  
2. **Persistent tab keys:** Allow developers to assign unique keys to tabs so that updating the title does not reset the selected tab.  
3. **Dynamic title updates without re-rendering:** Provide a mechanism for updating the displayed title independently of the tab component's internal state.  

**Example use case:**

```python
import streamlit as st

tab_titles = ["First", "Second", "Third"]
for i, title in enumerate(tab_titles):
    key = f"counter_{i}"
    if key not in st.session_state:
        st.session_state[key] = 0

dynamic_titles = [f"{title} (+{st.session_state[f'counter_{i}']})" 
                  for i, title in enumerate(tab_titles)]

tabs = st.tabs(dynamic_titles)  # Updating dynamic_titles resets selected tab

for i, tab in enumerate(tabs):
    with tab:
        st.write(f"### {tab_titles[i]}")
        if st.button("Increment counter", key=f"btn_{i}"):
            st.session_state[f"counter_{i}"] += 1
            st.rerun()
```

Currently, updating the `dynamic_titles` list causes the tabs to re-render and always select the first tab, which is not ideal for UX. Adding badge support or persistent tab keys would solve this problem elegantly.


### Why?

_No response_

### How?

For example:

```python
home, analytics, settings = st.tabs([
    st.Tab(title="Home", icon="🏠", badge=32),
    st.Tab(title="Analytics", icon="📊", badge=5),
    st.Tab(title="Settings", icon="⚙️")
])
```

Or just give option for key to stay persistent:
```python
home, analytics, settings = st.tabs(["Home", "Analytics", "Settings"], key="persistent_tabs")
```

### Additional Context

_No response_
issues.title: Add support for dynamic tab badges or persistent tab keys

### Summary

The newly launched `st.pdf` in version 1.49 renders the PDF in streamlit. I would like a few enhancements in it:

1. The current implementation renders PDF as images, hence it doesn't allow selection of text from the rendered PDF. This feature is useful for the user if s/he wants to copy some information from the rendered PDF.

2. There is an option to zoom in/out, but no option to download or print the rendered PDF. This feature is useful if the user needs a copy of the PDF.

3. There should be a width parameter and a default zoom percentage.

### Why?

_No response_

### How?

I've a simple workaround, taken from [`streamlit-extras`](https://pypi.org/project/streamlit-extras/) and it works well for me.

```python
def pdf_reader(file: str|bytes, base_url: str = '', width: int = None, height: int = 500) -> None:
    from streamlit.runtime import Runtime
    coordinates = st._main._get_delta_path_str()
    width = '100%' if width is None else f"{width}px"   
    runtime = Runtime.instance()
    pdf_url = base_url + runtime.media_file_mgr.add(file, "application/pdf", coordinates)
    html_content = f'<iframe src="{pdf_url}" style="width:{width}; height:{height}px;" type="application/pdf" frameborder="0"></iframe>'
    st.markdown(html_content, unsafe_allow_html=True)

```

### Additional Context

_No response_
issues.title: Add option to download the pdf file and copy text from rendered pdf in st.pdf

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

Currently, the pages argument to `st.navigation` supports two modes:
- List → renders all pages as flat top-level links
- Dict → renders each section as a dropdown (collapsible item) in the top navigation, even if the section contains only one page

From the docs:
“If you use position="top", each grouping will be a collapsible item in the navigation menu.” 

This means it is not possible to mix flat (single-page) items and grouped dropdowns at the same time in the top navigation.


### Why?

Many apps benefit from a hybrid layout:
- A few core pages should always be visible as flat links in the top bar.
- Additional related pages should live under dropdown groups.

Currently, the only way to achieve this is to hide the built-in navigation (position="hidden") and rebuild a custom header using `st.page_link` + `st.popover`. That works, but it means losing the convenience of st.navigation as a router.

### How?

support for a mixed dictionary format where the empty string "" acts as a “root” section for flat links:
```python
pages = {
    "": [   # Flat (root) links
        st.Page("flat1.py",  title="TitleF1", default=True),
        st.Page("flat2.py",  title="TitleF2"),
    ],
    "Nested": [  # Dropdown group
        st.Page("nested1.py",  title="Title1"),
        st.Page("nested2.py", title="Title2"),
    ],
}

pg = st.navigation(pages, position="top")
pg.run()
```

- Pages in "" (root) are rendered as flat top-level buttons.
- Pages in named sections are rendered in dropdowns, as today.
- Backward compatibility is preserved: lists work as before, dicts with only named sections work as before.


### Additional Context

https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/5889#issuecomment-2222697407
issues.title: Allow mixed flat + grouped navigation in st.navigation when position="top"

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

In BI dashboards, you often want to cross-filter between charts and/or dataframes. Building this in Streamlit via chart/dataframe selections isn't very straightforward. Could we find an easier solution?

### Why?

Two example use cases to illustrate the problem:

- Simple example: You have one chart and one dataframe. If you select some rows in the dataframe, the chart updates to show only those data points. If you select some data points in the chart, the dataframe updates to show only the corresponding rows. 
- Complex example: A dashboard with multiple charts. If you click on any chart, all the other charts update to only the data that was selected in the first chart. Ideally, this should also support then selecting data in a 2nd or 3rd chart to further drill down. 

It's possible to build this in Streamlit with chart/dataframe selections, but not very straightforward since:

1. You need to parse the selection and then manually filter the data in other visualizations based on what was selected. 
2. It's not easy to update a visualization that is "above" the one where data was selected, due to Streamlit's rerun model. You'd need to save all selections centrally in `st.session_state` and then update charts from there. 
3. The entire page will rerun on every selection, making this potentially slow. 

### How?

Probably needs a good amount of thinking but some rough ideas:

1. Allow passing the key of another element to `on_select`. This would then automatically sync that element whenever some data is selected in the current one. Or maybe it should even sync in both ways?

  ```python
  st.line_chart(..., key="chart1")
  st.dataframe(..., on_select="chart1")
  ```

2. Adding a command like `st.cross_filter` to cross filter between multiple charts/dataframes.

  ```python
  st.line_chart(..., key="chart1")
  st.plotly_chart(..., key="chart2")
  st.dataframe(..., key="dataframe")
  st.cross_filter("chart1", "chart2", "dataframe")
  ```

One big problem here is probably making sure all visualizations have access to the same data/can filter. E.g. if I have a pie chart showing the gender of all people, how can we make sure clicking on "Female" lets the other charts know how to filter their own data?

### Additional Context

_No response_
issues.title: Easier cross-filtering between charts/dataframes

issues.body: ### Checklist - [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests. - [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue. ### Summary We should be able to set the background color of a container (preferably in a fully-themable way) ### Why? When building a dashboard with elements of different shapes and sizes placed in a grid, a nice way to align the elements visually is by making the grid structure visible. Today this is done by setting `border=True` in the grid cells (`st.container`, `st.columns`, etc). This can work well at times, but other times those borders make the app too busy visually. (Or, to combat this, the developer makes the border colors fainter, but then the app loses its "shape" and becomes harder to parse) To solve this, one thing I found works well is to set the background color of the grid cells to a different value (usually white). **Here's an example of a sad dashboard with borders:** **And here's how it looks with white cells:** ### How? As with all API proposals, ignore the exact names used below. These proposals are more about the shape of the API than the exact tokens used. ### Idea 1: Cards Introduce a new st command (`st.card`): ```py with st.card(): ... ``` ```toml # config.toml [theme] cardBackgroundColor = "#ffffff" ``` ### Idea 2: Backgrounds in containers and columns Add a new boolean property to containers and columns, following the pattern already used for turning borders on/off: ```py with st.container(filled=True, border=True): ... with st.columns(2, filled=True, border=True): ... ``` ```toml # config.toml [theme] filledContainerBackgroundColor = "#ffffff" ``` ### Idea 3: Containers with importance levels This is similar to idea 2, but here we're have a string property that follows the `kind=` pattern already used in `st.button`: ```py with st.container(type="primary", border=True): ... with st.columns(2, type="primary", border=True): ... ``` ```toml # config.toml [theme] primaryContainerBackgroundColor = "#ffffff" ``` ### Idea 4: Containers with inline background color We could just allow users to pass the background color inline as a keyword argument. I'm not a fan of this idea at the moment since it can make apps hard to maintain, while also making it harder to share themes within a company, but I'm including it here for completeness: ```py with st.container(background_color="#ffffff", border=True): ... with st.columns(2, background_color="#ffffff", border=True): ... ``` ### Additional Context _No response_
issues.title: Ability to set background of st.container (or perhaps support for cards)
